To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lacto/neolocto-series GSLs are important for the clustering of GEM and tether-specific proteins.
lacto/neoloacto-series GSL synthesis by the enzyme β3Gn-T5 is important for B cell activation.

lacto/neolateo-glycoliplids play an important role as a negative regulatory factor for clustering of glycolipids in glycolipid microdomains, facilitating the formation of glycoipid-enrich microdomains and tethering of signaling molecules to the microdomains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biological functions of lactotriaoslyceramide (Lc₃Cer) synthetase, β1,3-GalNAc-transferase V (B3GNT5) in B cell signaling.
the biological functions of lactotriaosyllactosylceramide and lactotriaoslyceramide in B cells.
the in vivo functions of lacto- and neolacto-series glycoglycolipids in B cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lacto/neoglycolipids play a critical role in the formation of GEMs, facilitating B cell signaling and proliferation.
lacto/neolocto-series GSLs are involved in the regulation of B cell activation.
B3gnt-5-deficient mice are a good model to study the role of glycolipids in the formation of microdomains in the plasma membrane of lymphocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lacto/neo-lacto-series GSL synthesis in B cells may be important for the regulation of BCR signal strength and/or the regulation of the amount of BCR signal molecules.
the lacto/neolac-to-series GSLs are important for the formation of GEMs, and the formation of GMEs is important for the activation of B cells.
the lack of lacto/neolocto-series GSLs enhances the formation of GEMs, facilitating B cell responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lacto/neolocto-series GSLs regulate B cell activation through the regulation of the clustering of GEM and tethered proteins.
B3gnt-5 is a novel enzyme that regulates GEMs and that the lack of lacto/neoloacto-series GSL enhances B cell activation.
the lack of lacto/neolocto-series GSLs enhances the formation of GEMs, facilitating the clustering of signaling molecules and BCR signaling.
